concept.name: Capital loss
concept.definition: The loss realized when a capital asset is sold for less than its adjusted basis; per the IRS, you have a capital loss if you sell the asset for less than your adjusted basis. Capital losses offset capital gains, and if losses exceed gains, up to $3,000 ($1,500 if married filing separately) of the excess is deductible against ordinary income per year, with the remainder carried forward.
concept.intuition: Sell for less than you paid and you have a capital loss — painful, but it can shrink your tax bill by canceling out gains and a limited slice of ordinary income each year.
concept.mechanics: Losses are classified short-term or long-term by the same one-year holding rule as gains, then netted within and across categories on Schedule D. Net losses above the annual $3,000/$1,500 limit carry forward to later years indefinitely; losses on personal-use property (home, car) are not deductible, and losses on investment property repurchased within the 30-day window are deferred by the wash-sale rule.
concept.formula: Capital loss = adjusted basis - amount realized (when amount realized < adjusted basis); annual ordinary-income offset limit = lesser of $3,000 ($1,500 MFS) or total net loss.
concept.failure_modes: Taxpayers lose deductions by triggering wash sales, misclassifying holding periods, or failing to track carryovers across years; losses between related parties can be disallowed entirely, and the $3,000 annual cap means large realized losses may take many years to absorb.
concept.misconceptions: Capital losses cannot generally offset ordinary income beyond $3,000 per year — a $100,000 net loss does not wipe out $100,000 of salary; and losses on personal-use assets like your car or main home are never deductible.
concept.example: You sell stock bought for $10,000 for $6,000, realizing a $4,000 capital loss; with no gains that year you deduct $3,000 against ordinary income and carry $1,000 forward to the next year.

citations.source: IRS Topic No. 409, Capital Gains and Losses
citations.section: Limit on the deduction and carryover of losses
